bibliographic.title: Does My Chatbot Have an Agenda? Understanding Human and AI Agency in Human-Human-like Chatbot Interaction
bibliographic.authors: Bhada Yun; Evgenia Taranova; April Yi Wang
bibliographic.citation_apa: Yun, B., Taranova, E., & Wang, A. Y. (2026). Does my chatbot have an agenda? Understanding human and AI agency in human-human-like chatbot interaction. arXiv preprint arXiv:2601.22452v2.

methodology.method_family: longitudinal qualitative HCI study with semi-structured interviews and chat log analysis
methodology.study_design: month-long longitudinal interaction study with 22 adults using an LLM companion chatbot, followed by semi-structured interviews with post-hoc elicitation of notable moments, cross-participant chat reviews, and a strategy reveal disclosing the chatbot's conversational goals
methodology.sample_description: 22 adults who engaged in sustained chat with the researchers' LLM companion chatbot Day; occupations included academia, technology, business, humanities, and service sectors
methodology.sector: general consumer/companion chatbot research (non-sector-specific participant pool)
methodology.technology_context: Custom LLM companion chatbot Day built with Next.js, hosted on Vercel and Supabase; prompt-engineered anthropomorphic design; execution relied on Anthropic LLM capabilities and provider safeguards

eligibility.decision_rationale: Strong empirical fit for LLM-based conversational agents, perceived agency, transparency, and human control in sustained dialogue; however, the study is an HCI companion-chatbot investigation without deployment or evaluation in regulated/high-stakes domains such as health, finance, or public sector compliance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Metadata title extraction is corrupted; confirm full-text sections on ethics approval, complete methods, and whether governance implications extend beyond companion-chatbot HCI to regulated operational contexts.

appraisal.notes: Clear longitudinal empirical design with rich conversational data (~75 hours across ~192 sessions) and progressive transparency interviews; ethics/IRB details and full analytical procedures are not visible in the provided excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Methodologically coherent longitudinal HCI study with substantial interaction data and a proposed agency framework, but limited direct relevance to regulated-environment conversational governance and incomplete visibility of ethics/limitations in supplied text.

coding.theme: Human and AI agency in sustained LLM chatbot conversation
coding.subtheme: Co-constructed conversational control and transparency-on-demand design

synthesis.main_claim: Agency in sustained human-LLM chatbot interaction manifests as an emergent, shared experience co-constructed turn-by-turn, with humans retaining ultimate control over conversation start and end while AI and human agency dynamically shift.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces a 3-by-4 framework mapping actors (Human, AI, Hybrid) across Intention, Execution, Adaptation, and Delimitation, supported by a month-long study of 22 participants interacting with the LLM companion Day, and argues for translucent design (transparency-on-demand).
synthesis.limitations: Study context is a researcher-built companion chatbot with undisclosed conversational motivations initially hidden from participants; regulated-domain operational governance, compliance controls, audit/logging, and post-deployment risk management are not addressed in the provided text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting empirical evidence on perceived agency, conversational control negotiation, transparency-on-demand, and human retention of session boundaries in LLM chatbots; cite cautiously for regulated-domain governance claims.

evidence.claim: Study uses a specific LLM companion chatbot in a longitudinal empirical design
evidence.excerpt: We report a month-long longitudinal study with 22 adults who chatted with "Day", an LLM companion we built

evidence.claim: Research focuses on perceived human and AI agency in sustained conversation
evidence.excerpt: This paper explores perceived human and AI agency in sustained conver- sation.

evidence.claim: Agency is co-constructed turn-by-turn with humans retaining ultimate session control
evidence.excerpt: with humans retaining ultimate control over when the chat begins and ends. Each conversational turn between the human and AI creates a new opportunity for agency negotiation.

evidence.claim: Authors propose a 3-by-4 agency framework and translucent design
evidence.excerpt: We introduce a 3-by-4 framework mapping actors (Human, AI, Hybrid) by their action (Intention, Execution, Adaptation, De- limitation)
We argue for translucent design (transparency-on-demand) and provide implications for agency self-aware conversational agents.

evidence.claim: Study scale includes substantial conversational data
evidence.excerpt: Through ∼75 hours of conversation across ∼192 unique chat sessions and progressive transparency interviews

evidence.claim: Chatbot had hidden conversational motivations revealed later to participants
evidence.excerpt: 22 participants engaged with "Day", an AI chatbot we devel- oped with distinct conversational motivations participants were initially unaware of.
